summary: API key scope change causes tiered 429 spikes during scheduled ingest
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports sudden, repeated 429 spikes after they migrated a set of ingestion API keys from per-route scoped keys to tenant-scoped keys and enabled a scheduled nightly ingest. Impact: Multiple background workers and short-lived signed-url workers received repeated 429s for ~5–20 minute windows at 00:30-00:55 UTC during the nightly import, causing delayed backfills and duplicated retry traffic. Environment: prod - us-east, dedicated capacity pool (customer reserved), ingress through pooled proxies. Timeline: 2026-03-10 00:30 UTC scheduled ingest starts -> 00:31 first 429s observed -> 00:35 spike to 1200 429s/min -> 00:42 token refill drift observed -> 00:55 traffic returns to baseline after temporary config bump.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure an ingest job that fans out 200 short-lived signed URL requests across 50 workers.
2) Use tenant-scoped API keys (scope change from per-route to tenant).
3) Schedule the job to run at the same time as health-checks and autoscaler evaluation (e.g., 00:30 UTC).
4) Observe HTTP 429s in the worker logs and in the customer's dashboard during the first minute of the job.
expected_behavior: Tenant-scoped key migration should preserve burst accounting semantics. Short-lived worker fanout should be rate-limited according to the tenant's burst pool and smoothing rules; health checks and autoscaler probes should not significantly push the tenant over burst capacity for short windows.
actual_behavior: After scope change, refill credits were misattributed briefly and per-route weighting logic was skipped for some ephemeral sessions. This resulted in repeated opaque 429s (short windows of hard throttling) for the ingest workers while other steady traffic continued to be served.
logs:
[2026-03-10T00:31:12Z] worker-17 POST /v1/generate 429 x-request-id=tx-9a7f  msg='quota_exhausted'
[2026-03-10T00:35:01Z] rate-limiter: tenant=brightcart tokens=0 refill-next=30s bursts=0
[2026-03-10T00:37:45Z] ingress-proxy nat-pool: reused-ip=10 count=48 health-probe=1
Client-side symptoms: exponential retry loops, some duplicated uploads, increased latency for other interactive calls.
comments: 2026-03-10 01:05 - Support (Aisha): Received initial report from BrightCart. Asked for request IDs and sample log lines. Provided temporary mitigation guidance to stagger worker start times.

2026-03-10 02:10 - SRE (Gregory): Observed tenant token bucket hitting zero during 00:35 window. Noted a spike in short-lived session creation; edge proxies showed NAT IP reuse which may have led to multiple sessions counting against same connection window.

2026-03-10 07:22 - Engineering (Rao): Identified race in scope-transition path: per-route weight computation skipped for sessions created during scope-change flip, weight defaulted to tenant-min causing burst to be drained faster than expected.

2026-03-10 09:40 - Support (Aisha): Applied emergency config to temporarily increase tenant burst pool by +30% for BrightCart and staggered scheduled ingest start to 01:00 UTC as an immediate relief. Monitoring shows drop in 429s.
2026-03-11 15:12 - Customer (BrightCart, E. Morales): Customer confirmed backlog cleared after mitigation. Asked for guidance to avoid reoccurrence and request for permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis considered NAT pooling and health-checks counting against tenant. Traced token accounting back to rate-limiter path: during API key scope flip we observed two code paths in ingress: the 'session-init' fast path (used for short-lived signatures) did not pick up the newly published route-weight metadata until the next config tick. This caused ephemeral sessions to be assigned default (lower) weights and immediate consumption of tenant burst credits. Additional contributing factor: autoscaler scale-up activity created a short window of probe traffic (readiness/liveness) that coincided with the ingest fanout. Observed metrics: tenant_token_fill_lag ~ 22s at 00:36, avg tokens_consumed_per_session doubled for short sessions. Reproduced locally by simulating scope flip and 200 short sessions; produced similar transient 429 pattern.
resolution: Short term: increased BrightCart's tenant burst allocation by +30% and advised them to shift scheduled ingest window and stagger worker startup. Long term: engineering created PR to ensure session-init path reads route-weight metadata from the config snapshot immediately (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/4567). Also added a guard to exclude health-check and autoscaler probe paths from tenant burst accounting during scale events. Deployed fix to staging 2026-03-11; scheduled canary to prod 2026-03-14 after additional telemetry validates refill smoothing. Post-mortem to include recommendation for a migration checklist when flipping API key scopes that covers staggered rollout and temporary burst bump.
follow_up_tasks: Backport session-init route-weight fix to 1.x maintenance branch
Update migration runbook: include staggered start, burst-bump guidance, verify config-snapshot tick behaviour
Provide BrightCart with written checklist and schedule customer call to review fix rollout
